mapping.target: light-media internal/app/plugin_original_chat_download_notice.go, plugin_original_chat_media_download.go, plugin_original_chat_media_auto.go, search_download.go and job_completion.go
mapping.behavior: Separate material-fetch and downloader refusal notices, settle the exact failed attempt, and continue the ordered candidate loop only when no download was accepted.

native.kind: Exact indexed Linux amd64 worker in a native App, with owned loopback tracker, qBittorrent and Lark protocol peers
observations: A verified installed-worker interaction searched four sorted candidates. A tracker 404 emitted the source-shaped material failure card. The first Add returned a definite refusal and emitted a different, source-shaped Manual notice.

The rejected child finished once and released only its own reservation. The same ordered candidate loop fetched and attempted the next torrent. Its malformed acknowledgment produced a distinct unconfirmed card, kept its reservation and did not fetch the fourth resource.
The App persisted one failed attempt per actual Add, retained the unknown intent for reconciliation and wrote no download-accepted fact.

superseded_attempt.observation: The 404 notice appeared, but the synthetic torrent names did not reach downloader Add. The corrected fixture used known identity-matched file names and asserted candidate order. Host product logic was unchanged between attempts.

adaptations_and_open: Go distinguishes a malformed or ambiguous write acknowledgment from an explicit no-effect refusal. Unknown effects retain their download intent and reserve its scope instead of triggering another Add or a misleading definitive failure.

Current previews archive and pin the exact material. Older records with an empty archive reference can reacquire it using the guarded legacy path, which still differs in tracker first-download confirmation. No verified archive is substituted on recovery.
